newsitem.title: UK: Awakening consumers see minor metals trend higher.
newsitem.headline: Awakening consumers see minor metals trend higher.

text.p: Several industrial minor metals showed signs of breaking higher in the first quarter of 1997 as slumbering consumers awoke to a backdrop of low global stocks. Historically the minor metal sector finds robust consumer enquiry in the first quarter of the year.
"Overall stocks are at low levels and consumers are likely to start covering for their early 1997 commitments," one London trader commented.
Brisk upside business was reported in the antimony market amid the lack of Chinese offers, while cadmium, titanium, molybdendum and chrome firmed.
Referring to antimony one trader said, "The market is building up a head of steam and I believe we will see volatile trading over the coming year."
The London trader expected a range of between $2,000 and $2,500 a tonne to prevail during 1997.
Other sources roughly agreed but some said prices may have the potential to claw above $2,500 a tonne.
Near-term a lack of Chinese offers and low stocks should keep the market on the boil.
Stocks in Rotterdam were believed to be low and mostly held in the hands of China, a major producer, traders said.
"Consumers are slowly waking up to the fact that prices on low stocks are set to rise," a trader said.

But another said upside sentiment was overdone, believing demand from the consumer quarter was as yet not robust enough to lift prices significantly. "I have seen few signs of sustained buying interest from them (consumers)," this trader said. "Upside gusto has entered the market, which is clouding the general picture," the trader added. A flood of speculative money, buying interest from China and India, gave uptrending cadmium fresh impetus and traders said turnover was brisk. Several said turnover during the past week amounted to around 500 tonnes.
Cadmium is now poised to push higher as consumers start to replenish depleted stocks.
"The traditional New Year enthusiasm has chosen cadmium as the spectators' favourite target," a leading cadmium trader said.

The trader said prices after recovering from recent lows of $0.65 a pound could spike to the $1.00 level near-term, basis 99.99 percent material. Another noted that $0.95 was paid for forward metal for the same brand.
Demand from the aerospace industry and golf club manufacturers saw titanium sponge swing higher, while chrome also found renewed buying interest from the aircraft sector.
Demand from the highly technical industries such as aerospace and electronics and to a lesser extent the chemical industry sparked gains in molybdenum.
Like many of the other minor metals molybdenum is likely to find support from an expected growth in the hi-tech industries.
Cobalt's choppy trading in the second half of 1996 amid a battle between bulls and bears at present looks to have calmed.
But cobalt traders polled by Reuters said the two sides of the equation are unlikely to find middle ground in coming months.

"At the moment we seem to be in the eye of the storm regarding the trading strategies of the cobalt market but things look set to swirl soon," one said. Russian material drifted back on talk of a shipment from Dudinka of 160 tonnes of Norilsk production. Some market observers said that roughly 120 tonnes of the material had already been pre-sold to meet consumer commitments.
The bulls - in a point acknowledged by bears - believed the cold conditions around the Arctic circle may see little Russian material moved into Rotterdam until March.

High grade cobalt held steady against a backdrop of low stock, nearby tightness and aerospace demand. Traders said stocks in Rotterdam, Hong Kong and Baltimore were extremely low. Zaire a producer of high grade cobalt will be closely watched during the coming months.
Battles between government troops and rebels will continue to hold the spotlight. "A lot all depends who ends up holding the guns," one trader said.
But others said whatever the outcome from the central African country cobalt will remain nervous and prone to news and possible wide price movements

Bismuth refused to break out of recent ranges, though traders noted solid buying towards $3.00 a pound. Elsewhere, indium, iridium and germanium looked towards higher levels after downside pressure during a large majority of 1996.
